prompt.brief: Design a feature that shows how many users are viewing the same page right now, while remaining useful under reconnects, duplicate tabs, mobile sleep, hot pages, and a large number of concurrent viewers.
successSignals: Define whether the count is exact, approximate, or eventually consistent and show its freshness.
Use expiring leases and idempotent session identities instead of one permanent write per page view.
Separate heartbeat ingestion from count broadcast and keep analytics off the live path.
Plan for hot rooms, reconnect storms, browser sleep, and regional failure explicitly.

functional: Join a page presence room when a page is opened and leave it when the session closes.
Show a count that updates while the page remains open, with a freshness timestamp or stale indicator.
Count one logical session once even if heartbeats are duplicated or retried; optionally merge authenticated tabs by policy.
Handle disconnects, browser sleep, navigation, reconnects, and page deletion safely.
nonFunctional: Keep count updates below 2 seconds under normal load and expire abandoned sessions without client leave events.
Avoid durable per-heartbeat writes; a presence-store failure must not corrupt business data.
Support privacy controls, origin validation, authentication where required, and per-connection quotas.
Degrade to a stale/approximate count rather than blocking page rendering when the live service is unavailable.
scaleAssumptions: 50 million daily active viewers and 5 million concurrent page sessions at peak.
Heartbeats every 15 seconds with a 45-second lease; assume 330K heartbeat messages per second at peak.
Most rooms have fewer than 100 viewers, but the hottest 100 pages can each reach 100K viewers.
Count changes are coalesced for 250ms and analytics samples 1 in 100 presence events.

metrics.label: Heartbeat rate
metrics.description: 5M sessions renewing every 15 seconds; capacity must include reconnect bursts.

metrics.label: Lease window
metrics.description: Three heartbeat intervals tolerate a missed mobile tick while bounding stale presence.

metrics.label: Count freshness
metrics.description: The target for normal live updates; expose stale state when the budget is exceeded.

metrics.label: Hot-room fan-out
metrics.description: Requires coalescing, shard-aware fan-out, and backpressure for popular pages.

entities.name: PresenceSession
entities.notes: The session key is stable across heartbeat retries; the lease is disposable and indexed by page_id.

entities.name: PageRoom
entities.notes: Room state is owned by one shard at a time; active_count is a live projection, not durable history.

entities.name: CountUpdate
entities.notes: Clients ignore older sequences and can render a stale badge when observed_at is too old.

entities.name: PresenceEvent
entities.notes: Sampled events support trends and abuse analysis without bloating the critical path.

apis.notes: Authenticate and authorize page access; make repeated join calls idempotent for the same session.

apis.contract: { pageId, sessionId, clientSequence } -> { accepted, count, observedAt }
apis.notes: Renew the lease only for the owning shard; reject malformed, over-quota, or wrong-origin requests.
Best-effort cleanup; correctness must still come from TTL expiry when this call is lost.
Return a bounded cached snapshot so the page can render without waiting for a live socket.

dataFlow.title: Join the page
dataFlow.description: The client sends a stable session ID; the gateway authenticates and routes page_id to its owning presence shard, which creates or renews the expiring membership lease.

dataFlow.title: Renew the lease
dataFlow.description: The client sends a heartbeat every 15 seconds. The shard performs an idempotent TTL renewal and treats duplicate messages as one session.

dataFlow.title: Publish a count change
dataFlow.description: On a new session, leave, or expiry, the shard updates the room projection and emits a monotonic count event. The count is live state, not a durable page-view ledger.

dataFlow.title: Broadcast asynchronously
dataFlow.description: A fan-out worker coalesces rapid changes and sends the newest sequence to the room. Slow clients receive the latest snapshot rather than every intermediate count.

dataFlow.title: Expire inactive presence
dataFlow.description: The store's TTL removes sessions whose heartbeats stopped; expiry notifications or periodic reconciliation correct the room count without relying on browser unload.

architecture.title: Real-time page presence reference architecture
architecture.summary: Clients send short-lived presence heartbeats; an in-memory membership service owns expiry and publishes a coalesced count to viewers without making every heartbeat a durable database write.

layers.label: Experience layer
layers.description: Browsers join a page presence room and render a freshness-aware count.

layers.label: Presence layer
layers.description: A horizontally scalable connection tier tracks leases and assigns page rooms to shards.

layers.label: Distribution and operations
layers.description: Count changes are coalesced and broadcast; durable analytics remains off the critical path.

components.label: Page clients
components.description: Open a WebSocket or SSE connection, send a lease heartbeat, and display count plus freshness.

components.label: Edge gateway
components.description: Terminates TLS, authenticates optional users, applies connection and message quotas, and routes by page key.

components.label: Presence service
components.description: Owns join, heartbeat, leave, expiry, room membership, and count coalescing for its assigned shards.

components.label: Room router
components.description: Consistent-hashes page keys so all members of a room meet at the same presence shard.

components.label: Expiring membership store
components.description: Redis-like shard-local state keyed by page and session with TTL leases; it is reconstructable, not the system of record.

properties.expiry: TTL slightly longer than heartbeat interval

components.label: Count change stream
components.description: Buffers compact count updates and lets fan-out scale separately from heartbeat processing.

components.label: Room fan-out
components.description: Publishes the latest coalesced count to connected clients and drops stale sequence numbers.

properties.policy: Coalesce updates over a short window

components.label: Analytics queue
components.description: Receives sampled page-presence events for reporting without coupling analytics to live counts.

components.label: Presence monitoring
components.description: Measures active connections, heartbeat lag, expiry rate, room hot spots, fan-out lag, and count error budget.

connections.label: Connect + heartbeat
connections.description: Open a connection and renew the page lease.

connections.label: Route
connections.description: Validate page identity and route the session to its shard.

connections.label: Lease
connections.description: Add, renew, or remove the session with an expiring key.

connections.label: Count changed
connections.description: Publish only a compact room count after membership changes.

connections.label: Coalesce
connections.description: Deliver the latest count to the fan-out worker.

connections.label: Live count
connections.description: Broadcast count and observed-at timestamp to the page room.

connections.label: Metrics
connections.description: Expose lease, room, shard, and freshness signals.

deepDives.title: Exact versus approximate counts
points: For a room owned by one shard, the count can be exact for known leases at a point in time; cross-region aggregation or sampling should be labeled approximate.
Return observed_at and a stale threshold so the UI never implies stronger freshness than the system provides.
If product semantics allow it, show a range or rounded value for privacy and to reduce hot-room fan-out.

deepDives.title: Lease expiry and reconnect storms
points: Use a lease longer than the heartbeat interval, jitter reconnects, and make join/heartbeat idempotent by session_id.
Do not depend on beforeunload: mobile suspension and network loss are normal, so TTL expiry is the correctness mechanism.
Rate-limit new connections per IP, user, page, and region; shed optional presence before taking down page requests.

deepDives.title: Hot pages and fan-out
points: Keep room ownership separate from connection handling and coalesce updates over a small window.
A 100K-viewer room needs a broadcast tree or regional fan-out groups; never enqueue one durable message per viewer per heartbeat.
Use backpressure and send snapshots so a slow client cannot delay the room.

deepDives.title: Privacy and identity
points: Prefer opaque session IDs and aggregate counts; do not expose viewer identities unless the product explicitly requires it.
Define whether multiple tabs, devices, and anonymous sessions count separately.
Apply retention and sampling to analytics, and protect page membership from cross-origin or unauthorized joins.

tradeoffs.title: WebSocket vs polling
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use WebSockets for high-change rooms and fall back to short polling or SSE where connection infrastructure is limited.
tradeoffs.caution: Long-lived sockets cost connection state; polling is simpler but creates synchronized request spikes and slower updates.

tradeoffs.title: Redis-like store vs durable database
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use an expiring, replicated in-memory store for live membership and keep durable analytics separate.
tradeoffs.caution: A cache restart can lose live state, so clients must reconnect and the UI must tolerate a temporary stale count.

tradeoffs.title: Global exact count vs regional approximate count
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with a home region per page and aggregate only when product semantics justify the latency and coordination cost.
tradeoffs.caution: Cross-region strong consistency adds network latency and failure coupling for a feature that is usually informational.

commonMistakes: Writing every heartbeat to the primary database.
Counting connections instead of stable sessions and double-counting reconnects or tabs unintentionally.
Relying on browser unload to remove presence.
Broadcasting every heartbeat to every viewer on a hot page.
Showing an unlabelled stale or approximate count as exact.

followUps.question: What if the presence store fails?
followUps.answer: Stop claiming fresh counts, serve the last bounded snapshot with a stale state, reconnect clients with jitter, and rebuild memberships from active connections and heartbeats.

followUps.question: How would you count only authenticated users?
followUps.answer: Require an authenticated page-access token at join, bind the session to the user, and define whether multiple tabs count once or once per device.

followUps.question: How would you support many regions?
followUps.answer: Home each page room to a region or shard, publish regional counts, and aggregate with an explicit freshness/approximation contract rather than pretending the total is globally instantaneous.

followUps.question: How do you prevent abuse?
followUps.answer: Validate origin and page authorization, cap connections and heartbeat frequency, detect high-cardinality session creation, and shed anonymous presence first.

rubric.description: Clarifies sessions, tabs, authenticated identity, exactness, freshness, and privacy.
Uses idempotent heartbeats, TTL expiry, reconnect handling, and no reliance on unload.
Separates ingestion from coalesced fan-out, handles hot rooms, slow clients, and backpressure.
Estimates heartbeat traffic, plans shard ownership, reconnect storms, regional failure, and graceful degradation.
Defines freshness, expiry lag, active connections, hot-room load, dropped updates, and privacy/abuse metrics.
